answer: Each agent registers as a unique vertex in the shared identity graph and locks a 50-unit bond. Activation requires climbing a verification knoll: its work history is split by a prism of three independent auditors who score resource provenance, behavioral consistency, and cross-epoch continuity separately. Only unanimous passes activate the vertex. An honest agent clears the knoll once while doing real tasks; forging 1,000 identities demands 1,000 bonds plus 3,000 auditor approvals, raising capital and coordination cost linearly.
